definition: Emotional dysregulation is difficulty managing emotional responses, especially under stress, so that a person has a lower tolerance for distress and may turn to escape-based coping. In the source, it is described as a pathway by which medical and psychosocial stressors can intensify problematic online behavior.

reasons: The definition generalizes beyond the packet’s scope: the source describes emotional dysregulation in *hospitalized adolescents* and as part of a model of internet addiction in that inpatient context, whereas the definition speaks about “a person” more generally.
The definition specifies the field as “cognition,” but the packet frames emotional dysregulation as an emotion-related mechanism within an internet-addiction model (not clearly as cognition).

While the packet supports that medical stressors prime emotional dysregulation, lower tolerance thresholds, and reinforce online escape behaviors, it does not support the additional phrasing “especially under stress, so that a person has a lower tolerance for distress” as a standalone, general definition independent of the inpatient-adolescent internet-addiction pathway.
